name: The Family & Youth Institute
mission: TO STRENGTHEN AND EMPOWER INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION THAT PROMOTE: POSITIVE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, HEALTHY MARRIAGES, EFFECTIVE PARENTING, AND MENTAL HEALTH WELL-BEING.
theoryOfChange: The Family & Youth Institute (thefyi.org) explicitly mentions 'the fyi's theory of change' on its Research page. This page details their 'community-based participatory research approach,' which outlines how their projects are grounded in community collaboration and bridge community, research, and practice. The approach describes steps such as partnering with communities, engaging and integrating community voices, incorporating community perspectives on data, identifying practical solutions, and sharing benefits. It also highlights guiding principles for their research, including embracing resilience, celebrating intersectionality, and placing faith at the forefront. This framework explains how their activities are expected to lead to desired outcomes and impact.

rich_narrative.summary: The Family & Youth Institute provides research and educational resources to strengthen Muslim families and youth development. Founded in <cite id="5">2006</cite>, the organization works across mental health research, community education, and parenting support. In FY2024, the charity reported <cite id="2">$497,120 in total revenue</cite>, reflecting a 42% single-year revenue decline from FY2023 filings. Despite this contraction, the organization allocated <cite id="2">85.4% of expenses to program activities</cite>, maintaining direct service focus in community capacity building. It holds a <cite id="1">90/100 overall rating from Charity Navigator</cite> and receives support through <cite id="6">zakat-eligible contributions designated for fisabilillah</cite>. However, FY2023 financial reporting indicates <cite id="2">expenses exceeded annual revenue</cite>, drawing down existing net assets. Oversight metrics show executive compensation at <cite id="2">$80,000, representing 16.1% of revenue</cite>, which presents a governance consideration for a small-budget organization. Balance exists between its high program allocation and these underlying financial and operational factors.
